event.title: Sound Healing Meditation
event.description: Step into a deeper stillness inside the spacious and tranquil Buffalo Bayou Park Cistern. Offered in collaboration with UNIONisCREATION™, this meditation and sound experience invites guests into a space of resonance, restoration, and inner alignment. Each session unfolds as a shared moment of reflection, connection, and sound-guided stillness. Guests should bring their own cushions or mats. No food or drinks are allowed inside the Cistern. Cost: $20 PURCHASE TICKETS

event.title: Park Partners: The Rhythm of Our Roots
event.description: Join Rhythm of Our Roots, a free intergenerational community gathering presented by The Healing Portal Collective that transforms the park into a space for wellness, creativity, and connection. Experience guided Meridian Movement with Dr. Charlie Trinh, exploring gentle stretching, breathwork, and mindful movement inspired by Traditional Chinese Medicine. Relax into a restorative crystal bowl sound journey led by Blossom Legend, then join our signature community drum circle facilitated by Meesh Martinez, where rhythm becomes a shared language that brings people together. Designed for all ages and experience levels, this gathering offers accessible practices that support emotional well-being, self-expression, and community connection. Come as you are and rediscover the rhythm that connects us all. Presented as part of Buffalo Bayou Partnership’s Park Partners program, an initiative that connects neighborhood organizations with opportunities to activate parks, trails, and unique spaces along Buffalo Bayou. Cost Free Duration 12-5 PM Meeting Location Garver Park (705 Lockwood Dr) FREE REGISTRATION Meet the Team Dr. Charlie Trinh / Trinhquility is a Doctor of Acupuncture and Chinese Medicine, holistic healer, and community wellness advocate based in Houston. With a unique background in engineering and a deep-rooted calling toward Eastern medicine, Dr. Trinh integrates Traditional Chinese Medicine, movement practices, and energetic healing to support the body’s natural ability to restore balance. His work bridges ancient wisdom with modern understanding, emphasizing the connection between physical health, emotional well-being, and the surrounding environment. Through his practice, Trinhquility, Dr. Trinh has developed Meridian Movements, a mindful movement system designed to activate the body’s energetic pathways, improve circulation, and reconnect individuals to their natural rhythms. His vision for the Bayou project is to bring accessible, community-centered healing into nature, creating spaces where individuals can engage in intentional movement, breath, and awareness alongside the living ecosystem. By aligning human health with environmental harmony, Dr. Trinh aims to foster resilience, connection, and collective well-being within the Houston community. Meesh Martinez / Primitive Experience is a multimedia producer, filmmaker, and community arts facilitator based in Houston, Texas. An Austin native who grew up in Mexico City, Meesh holds a Bachelor’s degree in Cinematographic Language, a background that informs his work in visual storytelling, cultural documentation, and multimedia production. In Houston, Meesh collaborates with artists, organizations, and cultural institutions to produce video, photography, and digital media that document performances, community initiatives, and creative projects. His work focuses on amplifying cultural expression and strengthening connections between artists and communities. Meesh is also the founder of Primitive Experience, an initiative that creates immersive gatherings through drum circles, music, movement, and nature-based practices designed to foster connection, creativity, and collective well-being. Meesh is certified in facilitating drum circles for emotional regulation, using rhythm and group participation as tools for personal and community healing. In addition to his artistic and multimedia work, Meesh contributes to youth development programs and will be participating in the leadership and direction team for Peace Camp, supporting programming that nurtures creativity, emotional awareness, and community values for young participants. Meesh is also currently leading projects supported through grant funding that expand access to participatory arts experiences and cultural programming in Houston. Blossom Legend / Goddess Glow Birthing is a full-spectrum community doula, herbalist, chef, musician, and wellness facilitator dedicated to creating experiences that nourish the body, mind, and spirit. With more than a decade of experience in community wellness, culinary arts, and holistic care, her work weaves together ancestral wisdom, cultural traditions, nourishment, sound, and collective healing. Rooted in Afro-Caribbean traditions and a deep commitment to community care, Blossom creates spaces where people can slow down, reconnect with themselves, and experience healing in ways that are both accessible and transformative. As a chef of over twelve years, Blossom believes food is one of our most powerful medicines and a pathway to connection. Her culinary work focuses on nourishing meals, herbal preparations, botanical beverages, and community-centered dining experiences that celebrate the relationship between wellness, culture, and the earth. As an herbalist and doula, she supports individuals and families through life’s transitions, offering holistic care that honors the physical, emotional, and spiritual dimensions of well-being. At Rhythm of Our Roots, Blossom will guide a restorative sound bath experience designed to help participants release stress, regulate the nervous system, and reconnect with their own inner rhythm. Using healing vibrations, frequency harmonics, and meditative soundscapes, she invites participants into a state of deep rest, reflection, and renewal. Her approach is grounded in the belief that personal healing ripples outward, strengthening families, communities, and future generations.

event.title: Nature Walking Tour with Leave No Trace Experts
event.description: Learn about native plants and the insects that pollinate them along Buffalo Bayou! Follow along this discovery tour of Houston’s historic waterway ecosystem with Nancy Greig, founding director of the Cockrell Butterfly Center (now retired). An avid natural historian “jack of all trades”, she has particular interest in plants and insects, but birds, mammals, herpetofauna, and fish are all on her radar. At home she keeps busy with a butterfly garden, honey bee hives, and purple martin houses. Joining this month’s walk are special guests from Leave No Trace, who will be incorporating education about Leave No Trace principles into this nature walk. Cost 12 and over: $5 Children under 12: free Duration 90 minutes Meeting Location The Water Works in Buffalo Bayou Park (105-B Sabine St) REGISTER About Leave No Trace Leave No Trace is a supporter-based nonprofit organization dedicated to protecting the outdoors through science-based education that inspires responsible recreation. As more people visit parks, trails, and public lands, the pressure on our natural spaces grows. Leave No Trace works to ensure that everyone—no matter where they explore—has the knowledge and tools to enjoy nature while minimizing their impact.

event.title: Sunset Poetry with Undercurrents: Roberto Tejada
event.description: Enjoy an evening of poetry and immersive art, presented in conjunction with Undercurrents by Rafael Lozano-Hemmer in the Buffalo Bayou Park Cistern. The night begins with a poetry reading by one of the acclaimed writers who contributed to the installation and drinks on the terrace. Then, descend into the Cistern for a unique opportunity to experience Undercurrents with the writers. Cost $15 Duration 6:30-7:30 PM / 1 hour Location The reading begins on the Wortham Insurance Terrace above the Buffalo Bayou Park Cistern. (105-B Sabine St) PURCHASE TICKETS About Roberto Tejada Roberto Tejada is the author of poetry collections that include Mirrors for Gold (Krupskaya, 2006), Exposition Park (Wesleyan, 2010), Why the Assembly Disbanded (Fordham, 2022), and Carbonate of Copper (Fordham, 2025), longlisted for the PEN/Jean Stein Book Award. His writings on art and media history include National Camera: Photography and Mexico’s Image Environment (Minnesota, 2009), his work on the groundbreaking Mexican American artist Celia Alvarez Muñoz (UCLA/CSRC; Minnesota, 2009) and essay collections on Latin American and Latinx art and culture Still Nowhere in an Empty Vastness (Noemi, 2019), and the forthcoming Along the Diagonal: Art / Essays / América (Fordham, 2026). Awarded a John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation Fellowship in Poetry (2021) he is the Hugh Roy and Lillie Cranz Cullen Distinguished Professor at the University of Houston where he teaches Creative Writing and Art History.
event.excerpt: Experience an evening of poetry and immersive art with acclaimed writer Roberto Tejada, presented in conjunction with Undercurrents by Rafael Lozano-Hemmer.

Look for graceful herons, turtles, fish, and even an occasional alligator on the banks. Tours leave promptly on the hour beginning at 10 AM, 11 AM, 12 PM, and 1 PM. Cost Adults: $20 Children: $16 (ages 4-12) Departure Location Allen’s Landing (1019 Commerce St.) Weather permitting. Reservations Required. Children under the age of 4 are not permitted on the pontoon boat. PURCHASE TICKETS
event.excerpt: Escape within the heart of the city and glide along Buffalo Bayou! From the waterway, look for wildlife and unique views of Houston’s skyline.

event.title: Sound Healing Meditation
event.description: Step into a deeper stillness inside the spacious and tranquil Buffalo Bayou Park Cistern. Offered in collaboration with UNIONisCREATION™, this meditation and sound experience invites guests into a space of resonance, restoration, and inner alignment. Through gentle vibrations of singing bowls, wind chimes, and a gong, along with guided awareness, participants are supported in reconnecting body and mind. This series is more than meditation – it is a practice of listening, feeling, and returning to center within one of Houston’s most iconic, immersive spaces. Each session unfolds as a shared moment of reflection, connection, and sound-guided stillness. Guests should bring their own cushions or mats. No food or drinks are allowed inside the Cistern. Cost: $20 PURCHASE TICKETS
